questions.subject: science
questions.q: Burning of magnesium ribbon in air to form magnesium oxide is an example of which type of reaction?
questions.explanation: Magnesium and oxygen combine to form a single product, so it is a combination reaction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When an iron nail is dipped in copper sulphate solution, the blue colour of the solution slowly fades. This happens because
options: iron is less reactive than copper
iron reacts with the water in the solution
iron displaces copper and forms pale green iron sulphate
questions.explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper: Fe + CuSO4 gives FeSO4 + Cu.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the reaction Fe2O3 + 2Al gives Al2O3 + 2Fe, used to join railway tracks, which substance is oxidised?
questions.explanation: Aluminium gains oxygen to form aluminium oxide, so it is oxidised, while iron(III) oxide loses oxygen and is reduced.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Quicklime reacts vigorously with water to form
questions.explanation: CaO + H2O gives Ca(OH)2, slaked lime, releasing a lot of heat.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sodium sulphate solution is mixed with barium chloride solution and a white precipitate forms. The reaction is a
questions.explanation: The two compounds exchange ions to give BaSO4 (white precipitate) and NaCl, which is double displacement.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Silver chloride kept in a white dish in sunlight turns grey. This is because
options: light decomposes it into silver and chlorine
it reacts with oxygen to form silver oxide
it absorbs moisture from the air
it melts in the heat of the Sun
questions.explanation: Sunlight causes a photochemical decomposition, 2AgCl giving 2Ag + Cl2, and the grey colour is silver metal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a balanced chemical equation and why must a chemical equation be balanced?
questions.answer: A balanced chemical equation has the same number of atoms of each element on both sides. It is needed because, by the law of conservation of mass, mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
keyPoints: Equal number of atoms of each element on both sides
questions.explanation: Balancing makes the equation obey conservation of mass.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Distinguish between exothermic and endothermic reactions, giving one example of each.
questions.answer: In an exothermic reaction heat is released, for example burning of natural gas or respiration. In an endothermic reaction heat is absorbed, for example decomposition of calcium carbonate on heating.
questions.explanation: The difference lies in whether the reaction gives out or takes in heat.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a strong acid?
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid ionises almost completely in water, while the others are weak organic acids.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A solution turns red litmus paper blue. The solution is most likely
questions.explanation: Bases turn red litmus blue.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The soil in a farmer's field is too acidic for the crop. Which substance is most suitable to add to it?
questions.explanation: A base such as quicklime or slaked lime neutralises the excess acid in the soil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The chemical name of baking soda is
questions.explanation: Baking soda is NaHCO3, sodium hydrogencarbonate.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Plaster of Paris is prepared by heating which substance at 373 K?
questions.explanation: Heating gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O) at 373 K gives plaster of Paris (CaSO4.1/2 H2O).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Dry HCl gas does not change the colour of dry blue litmus paper, but moist blue litmus turns red. Why?
options: HCl produces H+ ions only in the presence of water
Dry litmus paper is damaged by the gas
HCl behaves as a base when it is dry
Water acts as a catalyst for litmus
questions.explanation: Acidic behaviour is due to H+ ions, which are released only when HCl dissolves in water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the pH scale? What is the pH of a neutral solution?
questions.answer: The pH scale is a scale from 0 to 14 that measures how acidic or basic a solution is. A neutral solution such as pure water has pH 7; below 7 is acidic and above 7 is basic.
questions.explanation: pH indicates hydrogen ion concentration on a convenient scale.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does taking an antacid tablet give relief from acidity in the stomach?
questions.answer: Acidity is caused by excess hydrochloric acid in the stomach. An antacid contains a mild base such as magnesium hydroxide, which neutralises the extra acid.
keyPoints: Excess HCl in stomach causes acidity
questions.explanation: A base neutralises the acid, relieving the discomfort.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the only common metal that is liquid at room temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these metals reacts most vigorously with cold water?
questions.explanation: Sodium is highly reactive and reacts violently with cold water, releasing hydrogen.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sodium and potassium are stored under kerosene oil because
options: they react very vigorously with oxygen and moisture in air
they are insoluble in kerosene only
they are too heavy to keep in air
questions.explanation: They are so reactive that they could catch fire in air, so kerosene keeps them away from oxygen and moisture.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Brass is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Brass is made from copper and zinc.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The property of metals by which they can be drawn into thin wires is called
questions.explanation: Ductility is the ability to be drawn into wires; malleability is being beaten into sheets.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A gold ornament found in an ancient ruin is still shiny, but iron tools found with it are badly rusted. The best reason is that
options: gold is a better conductor than iron
gold is very unreactive and does not corrode easily
questions.explanation: Gold is low in the reactivity series, so it does not react with air or moisture.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Define ore and gangue.
questions.answer: An ore is a mineral from which a metal can be extracted profitably. Gangue is the earthy impurities such as sand and soil present in the ore.
keyPoints: Ore is a mineral that yields metal profitably
Gangue is the impurities in the ore
questions.explanation: Gangue must be removed before extracting the metal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Aluminium is a reactive metal, yet aluminium utensils last long. Explain.
questions.answer: Aluminium forms a thin, tough layer of aluminium oxide on its surface when exposed to air. This layer is unreactive and protects the metal beneath from further corrosion.
keyPoints: A thin oxide layer forms on the surface
questions.explanation: The protective oxide film stops further corrosion.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The valency of carbon is
questions.explanation: Carbon has four electrons in its outer shell and forms four covalent bonds.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is an unsaturated hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: C2H4 (ethene) has a carbon-carbon double bond, so it is unsaturated.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Soap helps remove oily dirt from clothes because
options: soap converts the oil to a gas
soap reacts with dirt to form an insoluble salt
soap dissolves the dirt like a solvent
soap molecules form micelles with the oil trapped inside
questions.explanation: The hydrocarbon tails of soap dissolve in oil while the ionic heads face water, forming micelles that are rinsed away.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The functional group present in alcohols is
questions.explanation: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl group, -OH.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate, the gas evolved is
questions.explanation: Acids react with carbonates to release carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why do unsaturated hydrocarbons usually burn with a sooty yellow flame while saturated ones burn with a clean blue flame?
options: Unsaturated ones have a higher proportion of carbon that burns incompletely, giving soot
questions.explanation: A higher carbon percentage leads to incomplete combustion and soot in unsaturated compounds.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name the first four members of the alkane series and write their formulae.
questions.answer: Methane CH4, ethane C2H6, propane C3H8 and butane C4H10.
questions.explanation: Alkanes follow the general formula CnH(2n+2).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a homologous series? Mention two features of it.
questions.answer: A homologous series is a family of organic compounds with the same functional group in which successive members differ by a CH2 unit. Members have similar chemical properties and show a gradual change in physical properties.
keyPoints: Similar chemical properties and gradation in physical properties
questions.explanation: Homologous series organise the study of carbon compounds.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Photosynthesis takes place in which part of a plant cell?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which traps light energy.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The enzyme in saliva that begins the digestion of starch is
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase breaks starch down into sugar in the mouth.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a plant that has gone without water for many days the stomata close. This is because the guard cells
options: lose water and shrink, closing the pore
questions.explanation: Guard cells open the pore when they take in water and close it when they lose water, reducing water loss.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The basic filtering unit of the kidney is the
questions.explanation: Each kidney has many nephrons that filter blood to form urine.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The blood vessel that carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart is the
questions.explanation: The pulmonary vein returns oxygen-rich blood to the left atrium.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Arteries have thicker, more elastic walls than veins because
options: arteries contain valves to stop backflow
blood leaves the heart through them under high pressure
arteries only carry blood to the lungs
questions.explanation: Blood pumped out of the heart is under high pressure, so artery walls must withstand it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write the process of photosynthesis in words and mention the conditions needed.
questions.answer: Carbon dioxide and water, in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll, are converted into glucose (carbohydrate) and oxygen is released.
keyPoints: Carbon dioxide and water are raw materials
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is how green plants make their food.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is the small intestine long and covered with villi?
questions.answer: The length gives enough time for complete digestion and absorption. Villi are finger-like projections that increase the surface area for absorbing digested food and are richly supplied with blood vessels.
keyPoints: Length allows complete digestion and absorption
questions.explanation: The structure suits absorption of food.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which part of a neuron receives information from other cells?
questions.explanation: Dendrites receive the signal and pass it to the cell body.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A reflex action such as pulling the hand away from a hot object is mainly controlled by the
questions.explanation: Reflex arcs are processed in the spinal cord, which saves time.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: After a heavy meal rich in sugar, blood glucose rises. The body responds mainly by
options: secreting adrenaline from the adrenal glands
secreting growth hormone from the pituitary
questions.explanation: Insulin from the pancreas lowers blood sugar level.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which plant hormone is mainly responsible for the bending of a shoot towards light?
questions.explanation: Auxin collects on the shaded side and makes cells there grow longer, bending the shoot toward light.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Iodine is needed in the diet to make which hormone?
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland to make thyroxine; lack of it causes goitre.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A seedling is placed horizontally. After a few days its root bends downward and shoot bends upward. This shows
options: geotropism, with root positive and shoot negative
questions.explanation: Roots grow towards gravity (positive geotropism) and shoots away from it (negative geotropism).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name the three main parts of the human brain.
questions.answer: The forebrain (including the cerebrum), the midbrain and the hindbrain (cerebellum, pons and medulla).
questions.explanation: These are the three main regions of the brain.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a reflex action? Give one example.
questions.answer: A reflex action is a sudden, automatic response to a stimulus that does not need thinking. For example, quickly withdrawing your hand on touching a hot object.
keyPoints: Quick automatic response to a stimulus
questions.explanation: Reflex actions protect the body quickly.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following reproduces by budding?
questions.explanation: Hydra grows buds on its body that detach as new individuals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Binary fission in Amoeba produces
questions.explanation: The cell splits into two daughter Amoebae.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Plants grown by vegetative propagation are very similar to the parent plant because
options: only one parent is involved and no gametes fuse
questions.explanation: Without fusion of gametes, there is little variation from the parent.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The male reproductive part of a flower is the
questions.explanation: The stamen has an anther that produces pollen.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In human females fertilisation normally takes place in the
questions.explanation: The sperm meets the egg in the oviduct (fallopian tube).

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is the placenta important during pregnancy?
options: It passes nutrients and oxygen from the mother to the embryo and removes its wastes
It stores eggs for later use
It protects the uterus from infection only
questions.explanation: The placenta has villi that exchange materials between mother and embryo.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is pollination? Name two agents of pollination.
questions.answer: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma of a flower. It is carried out by agents such as wind, insects, water or birds.
keyPoints: Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma
Two agents such as wind and insects
questions.explanation: Pollination must happen before fertilisation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Mention two methods by which unwanted pregnancy can be prevented.
questions.answer: Barrier methods such as a condom, oral contraceptive pills, a copper-T (intrauterine device), or surgical methods such as vasectomy and tubectomy.
keyPoints: Barrier method such as a condom
Another method such as pills, IUD or surgery
questions.explanation: Contraceptive methods prevent fertilisation or implantation.

crossCheck.note: Pills and copper-T (IUD) are not barrier methods; the answer mislabels them as barrier methods.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Who is known as the father of genetics?
questions.explanation: Mendel's experiments on garden pea established the basic rules of inheritance.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A pure tall pea plant (TT) is crossed with a pure dwarf plant (tt). All plants of the F1 generation are
questions.explanation: All F1 plants are Tt, and tallness is dominant.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A couple already has three daughters. What is the chance that their fourth child will be a girl?
questions.explanation: Each child has an independent 50% chance of being a girl, because the sperm carries X or Y with equal probability.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How many pairs of chromosomes are present in a human body cell?
questions.explanation: A human cell has 46 chromosomes, which is 23 pairs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation of a monohybrid cross is
questions.explanation: Three plants show the dominant trait for every one showing the recessive trait.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a dihybrid cross Mendel obtained a 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio in F2. This shows that
options: the two traits always travel together
both traits are controlled by the same gene
the two traits are inherited independently of each other
questions.explanation: New combinations of traits appear, so the traits assort independently.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What are dominant and recessive traits?
questions.answer: A dominant trait is the one that appears in the F1 generation when two contrasting traits are crossed. A recessive trait is the one that is hidden in F1 and reappears in F2.
keyPoints: Recessive trait is hidden in F1 and appears in F2
questions.explanation: This is the result of Mendel's monohybrid cross.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are variations important for a species?
questions.answer: Variations help some individuals survive when the environment changes, such as in temperature or food supply. These individuals reproduce and pass on useful traits, so the species is not wiped out.
questions.explanation: Variation gives species a better chance of survival.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which type of mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
questions.explanation: A convex mirror gives an erect image and a wide field of view.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The radius of curvature of a spherical mirror is 24 cm. Its focal length is
questions.explanation: Focal length is half the radius of curvature, f = R/2 = 12 cm.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror. The image formed is
options: real, inverted and the same size, at the centre of curvature
real, inverted and magnified, beyond the centre of curvature
real, inverted and diminished, between F and C
questions.explanation: When the object is at C, the image is at C, real, inverted and equal in size.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of power of a lens is
questions.explanation: Power is 1/f with f in metres, and its unit is the dioptre.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The refractive index of a medium is equal to
options: speed of light in the medium divided by speed in vacuum
speed of light in the medium multiplied by speed in vacuum
speed of light in vacuum multiplied by the wavelength
speed of light in vacuum divided by speed in the medium
questions.explanation: n = c/v, the ratio of the speed in vacuum to the speed in the medium.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A concave lens has a focal length of 25 cm. Its power is
questions.explanation: P = 1/f = 1/(-0.25 m) = -4 D, negative for a concave lens.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State the two laws of reflection of light.
questions.answer: The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.
keyPoints: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection
Incident ray, reflected ray and normal in the same plane
questions.explanation: These laws apply to all reflecting surfaces.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two uses of concave mirrors.
questions.answer: They are used in torches and vehicle headlights to send out parallel beams, as shaving mirrors to see a magnified face, by dentists to see enlarged images of teeth, and in solar furnaces.
questions.explanation: A concave mirror can converge light or give a magnified erect image at close range.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: Which part of the eye controls the size of the pupil?
questions.explanation: The iris is a muscular diaphragm that changes pupil size to regulate light entering the eye.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: Myopia (short-sightedness) is corrected using
questions.explanation: A concave lens diverges the rays so that the image falls on the retina.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: In a myopic eye, the image of a distant object is formed
questions.explanation: The eyeball is too long or the lens too converging, so the focus is in front of the retina.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The splitting of white light into its component colours is called
questions.explanation: Dispersion happens because different colours bend by different amounts in a prism.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The sky appears blue mainly because
options: it reflects the colour of the sea
air molecules scatter shorter wavelengths more strongly
questions.explanation: Blue light has a shorter wavelength and is scattered more by the very small particles in air.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The Sun appears red at sunrise and sunset because
options: its light travels a longer path in the atmosphere, so blue is scattered away and red reaches us
the Sun becomes cooler at those times
the atmosphere absorbs all blue light
the Sun is closer to the Earth
questions.explanation: On the long path through air, most blue light is scattered out of the beam, leaving red.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: What is meant by the power of accommodation of the eye? What is the near point of a normal eye?
questions.answer: It is the ability of the eye lens to change its focal length so that both near and distant objects are seen clearly. The near point of a normal eye is about 25 cm.
keyPoints: Change in focal length of the eye lens
questions.explanation: The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the lens.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: Why do stars twinkle but planets do not?
questions.answer: Starlight is refracted by the changing layers of the atmosphere, and a star is a point source so its apparent position and brightness flicker. A planet is a larger extended source, so the variations average out.
keyPoints: Planets are extended sources so effects average out
questions.explanation: Twinkling is an effect of the atmosphere.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of electric current is
questions.explanation: Current is measured in amperes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A 12 V battery drives a current of 3 A through a resistor. The resistance is

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Resistors of 2 ohm, 3 ohm and 6 ohm are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A device used to measure electric current in a circuit is the
questions.explanation: An ammeter is connected in series to measure current.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: If the length of a wire is doubled while its material and thickness stay the same, its resistance
questions.explanation: Resistance is directly proportional to length.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An electric heater of 1000 W is used for 2 hours. The energy consumed is
questions.explanation: Energy = power x time = 1 kW x 2 h = 2 kWh.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State Ohm's law.
questions.answer: At constant temperature, the potential difference across the ends of a conductor is directly proportional to the current through it, so V = IR.
questions.explanation: The constant of proportionality is the resistance.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is tungsten used to make the filament of electric bulbs?
questions.answer: Tungsten has a very high melting point, so it does not melt at the high temperature of a glowing filament, and its high resistivity makes it heat up and glow strongly.
questions.explanation: The filament must stay solid while white hot.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Outside a bar magnet, magnetic field lines go from
options: the north pole to the south pole
the south pole to the north pole
questions.explanation: By convention, field lines emerge from the north pole and enter the south pole.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A straight conductor carrying an electric current produces
questions.explanation: Oersted showed that a current produces a magnetic field around the wire.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the thumb points in the direction of
options: the force or motion of the conductor
questions.explanation: The forefinger shows the field, the middle finger shows the current and the thumb shows the force.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A device that converts electrical energy into mechanical energy is the
questions.explanation: An electric motor uses the force on a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When a magnet is moved into a coil connected to a galvanometer the needle deflects. This phenomenon is called
questions.explanation: A changing magnetic field induces a current in the coil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A magnet is held at rest inside a coil connected to a galvanometer and there is no deflection. This is because
options: the magnet has lost its magnetism
there is no change of magnetic field through the coil, so no current is induced
galvanometers work only with alternating current
questions.explanation: Induction needs a changing magnetic field through the coil.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write two properties of magnetic field lines.
questions.answer: Field lines are closed curves that go from the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet. They never cross each other, and a closer spacing of lines shows a stronger field.
keyPoints: Closed curves from north to south outside the magnet
questions.explanation: Field lines are a way to picture the magnetic field.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the function of a split ring commutator in a DC electric motor?
questions.answer: The split ring commutator reverses the direction of current in the coil after every half rotation. This keeps the force on the coil in the same sense so that it continues to rotate in one direction.
keyPoints: Reverses current direction every half turn
Coil keeps rotating in the same direction
questions.explanation: Without it the coil would just oscillate.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a producer in a food chain?
questions.explanation: Green plants make their own food by photosynthesis.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The flow of energy in a food chain is
questions.explanation: Energy flows from producers to consumers and is not returned to the Sun.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Food chains rarely have more than four or five trophic levels because
options: energy is lost at each level so very little is left for higher levels
questions.explanation: Only about 10 percent of energy passes to the next level.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: About what percentage of the energy is passed on from one trophic level to the next?
questions.explanation: This is the 10 percent law of energy transfer.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which group of chemicals is mainly responsible for damaging the ozone layer?
questions.explanation: CFCs release chlorine in the stratosphere, which breaks down ozone.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A pesticide sprayed on crops is later found in high concentration in hawks that feed on small birds. This is called
questions.explanation: Non-biodegradable chemicals build up in higher trophic levels.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What are decomposers? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Decomposers break down dead plants and animals into simple substances that return to the soil. Examples are bacteria and fungi.
questions.explanation: They recycle nutrients.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Differentiate between biodegradable and non-biodegradable substances with one example each.
questions.answer: Biodegradable substances such as vegetable peels and paper are broken down by microorganisms. Non-biodegradable substances such as plastics and glass are not, so they remain in the environment for a very long time.
questions.explanation: The difference lies in whether decomposers can break them down.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The reaction CaCO3 giving CaO + CO2 on heating is a
questions.explanation: One compound breaks down into two simpler substances, so it is decomposition.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Green crystals of ferrous sulphate are heated strongly. A smell like burning sulphur is noticed and a reddish-brown solid is left. The solid is
questions.explanation: Ferrous sulphate decomposes into ferric oxide (Fe2O3), sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the electrolysis of acidified water, compared with the tube collecting oxygen, the tube collecting hydrogen contains
options: four times the volume of gas
questions.explanation: Water is H2O, so 2H2O gives 2H2 + O2, so hydrogen and oxygen are in a 2:1 ratio by volume.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The process in which food containing fats and oils becomes foul-smelling and tasting after a long time is called
questions.explanation: Oxidation of fats and oils causes rancidity.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Manufacturers flush packets of potato chips with which gas to prevent rancidity?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is unreactive, so it keeps oxygen away from the chips.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When lead nitrate is heated strongly in a boiling tube, brown fumes are seen. These fumes are of
questions.explanation: Lead nitrate decomposes into lead oxide, brown nitrogen dioxide and oxygen.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is corrosion? Give one example.
questions.answer: Corrosion is the slow eating away of a metal by air, moisture or chemicals on its surface. The rusting of iron, which forms a reddish-brown coating, is an example.
keyPoints: Gradual damage of a metal by action of air or moisture
questions.explanation: Corrosion damages objects made of metals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is respiration considered an exothermic process?
questions.answer: In respiration, glucose is oxidised in the cells to carbon dioxide and water with the release of energy. Since heat energy is given out, it is an exothermic reaction.
questions.explanation: Energy released in respiration keeps the body working and warm.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which acid is present in vinegar?
questions.explanation: Vinegar is a dilute solution of acetic (ethanoic) acid.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When an electric current is passed through aqueous sodium chloride, sodium hydroxide and chlorine form along with
questions.explanation: This is the chlor-alkali process, which gives NaOH, Cl2 and H2.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Universal indicator turns solution P red, Q green, R blue-violet and S orange. Which solution is closest to neutral?
questions.explanation: Green with universal indicator corresponds to about pH 7.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Washing soda is
questions.explanation: Washing soda is hydrated sodium carbonate with 10 molecules of water of crystallisation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Passing chlorine gas over dry slaked lime produces
questions.explanation: Chlorine reacts with dry slaked lime to form bleaching powder.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Baking soda is added to cake batter and the cake becomes soft and spongy on baking. This is because baking soda
options: releases carbon dioxide on heating, which makes the batter rise
reacts to form oxygen that sweetens the cake
increases the sugar content of the batter
questions.explanation: Heating releases carbon dioxide gas, which gets trapped and makes the cake rise.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is an indicator? Name two natural indicators.
questions.answer: An indicator is a substance that shows by a change in colour whether a solution is acidic or basic. Litmus and turmeric (also red cabbage juice or China rose petals) are natural indicators.
keyPoints: Changes colour in acid or base
Two natural indicators such as litmus and turmeric
questions.explanation: Indicators help identify acids and bases.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What do you observe when carbon dioxide is passed through lime water for a short time and then for a long time? Give reasons.
questions.answer: Lime water first turns milky because insoluble calcium carbonate forms. On passing excess carbon dioxide the milkiness disappears since soluble calcium hydrogencarbonate is formed.
questions.explanation: Both products form from the reaction of lime water with CO2.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following non-metals is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Graphite, a form of carbon, conducts electricity.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which gas is evolved when most metals react with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Metals displace hydrogen from acids.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following metals will displace copper from copper sulphate solution?
questions.explanation: Zinc is above copper in the reactivity series, while silver, gold and mercury are below it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When metals burn in oxygen they generally form
questions.explanation: Metal oxides are formed, which are usually basic.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Ionic compounds have high melting points because
options: of strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions
of covalent bonds between the atoms
questions.explanation: A lot of energy is needed to overcome the strong attraction between ions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sodium chloride does not conduct electricity as a solid but does when molten. The reason is that
options: electrons are free to move in the solid
atoms are free to move in the solid
ions become free to move when molten
questions.explanation: In the solid, ions are fixed in position, and on melting they can carry current.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is an alloy? Give one example with its components.
questions.answer: An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of a metal with other metals or non-metals. For example, steel is iron with a small amount of carbon, and brass is copper and zinc.
keyPoints: Homogeneous mixture of metal with other elements
questions.explanation: Alloys often have better properties than pure metals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain the formation of sodium chloride by transfer of electrons.
questions.answer: A sodium atom loses its one outer electron to become a Na+ ion, and a chlorine atom gains that electron to become a Cl- ion. The oppositely charged ions attract each other and form an ionic bond in NaCl.
keyPoints: Sodium loses one electron to form Na+
Chlorine gains one electron to form Cl-
questions.explanation: Both ions attain a stable noble-gas arrangement.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The formula CH3COOH represents
questions.explanation: CH3COOH is ethanoic (acetic) acid.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid in the presence of a little concentrated sulphuric acid to form a sweet-smelling compound called
questions.explanation: This is esterification, and the product is ethyl ethanoate.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Diamond is very hard whereas graphite is soft and slippery. This is because
options: diamond has a greater mass of carbon
carbon atoms are arranged differently in the two
questions.explanation: Diamond has a rigid three-dimensional network, while graphite has layers that slide over each other.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The general formula of alkenes is
questions.explanation: Alkenes have one double bond and follow CnH2n.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In an ethene molecule the two carbon atoms are joined by a
questions.explanation: Ethene, C2H4, has a carbon-carbon double bond.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Carbon compounds generally have low melting and boiling points because
options: the bonds between their atoms are weak
the forces of attraction between their molecules are weak
questions.explanation: Covalent compounds are made of molecules held together by weak intermolecular forces.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is catenation?
questions.answer: Catenation is the ability of carbon atoms to join with other carbon atoms to form long chains, branched chains and rings.
keyPoints: Carbon atoms bond to other carbon atoms
questions.explanation: This property accounts for the huge number of carbon compounds.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How would you distinguish between ethanol and ethanoic acid by a simple chemical test?
questions.answer: Add a little sodium hydrogencarbonate to each. Ethanoic acid gives brisk effervescence of carbon dioxide, while ethanol gives none. Blue litmus turning red also identifies the acid.
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Exchange of gases between air and blood in the lungs takes place in the
questions.explanation: Alveoli are thin-walled air sacs surrounded by blood capillaries.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Yeast respires anaerobically to produce
questions.explanation: Fermentation by yeast converts glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: After a sudden sprint, an athlete's muscles may cramp. This is because
options: excess oxygen collects in the muscle
carbon dioxide dissolves in the muscle
lactic acid builds up when glucose is broken down without enough oxygen
questions.explanation: In oxygen-starved muscle, pyruvate is converted to lactic acid.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Bile juice is produced by the
questions.explanation: Bile is made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In humans haemoglobin in the blood mainly transports
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin in red blood cells carries oxygen.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Aquatic animals breathe at a much faster rate than terrestrial animals because
options: water contains more oxygen than air
the amount of dissolved oxygen in water is quite low compared with air
aquatic animals do not have lungs
questions.explanation: Water has little dissolved oxygen, so more water must pass over gills.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name the two modes of nutrition with one example of each.
questions.answer: Autotrophic nutrition, in which organisms make their own food, as in green plants. Heterotrophic nutrition, in which organisms depend on others for food, as in humans or a cow.
questions.explanation: Organisms are classified by how they obtain food.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is double circulation of blood necessary in humans?
questions.answer: In double circulation, blood passes through the heart twice in one complete round. It keeps oxygenated and deoxygenated blood separate, so oxygen is supplied efficiently, which is needed by warm-blooded animals with high energy needs.
keyPoints: Blood passes twice through the heart
Oxygenated and deoxygenated blood stay separate
Efficient oxygen supply for high energy needs
questions.explanation: This design supports a high rate of respiration.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which hormone is called the emergency hormone because it prepares the body for fight or flight?
questions.explanation: Adrenaline increases heart rate and breathing in emergencies.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The part of the brain responsible for posture and balance of the body is the
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movements and balance.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A person touches a hot pan and pulls the hand away before feeling pain. This is because
options: the signal is processed in the spinal cord without waiting for the brain
the brain is not connected to the hand
impulses travel faster in the brain
questions.explanation: The reflex arc passes through the spinal cord, giving a quick response.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The gap between two neurons is called a
questions.explanation: Impulses cross the synapse with the help of chemicals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Growth hormone is secreted by the
questions.explanation: The pituitary, the master gland, secretes growth hormone.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The tendrils of a pea plant coil around a support when they touch it. This movement is a response to
questions.explanation: The side not in contact grows faster, which makes the tendril coil around the support.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a stimulus and what is a receptor?
questions.answer: A stimulus is a change in the environment, such as light or heat, to which an organism responds. A receptor is a specialised cell or organ, such as the eye or skin, that detects the stimulus.
keyPoints: Stimulus is a change in the environment
questions.explanation: Receptors start the response in the nervous system.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name two plant hormones that promote growth and two that inhibit growth.
questions.answer: Auxin and gibberellins (also cytokinins, which promote cell division) promote growth. Abscisic acid and ethylene inhibit growth; abscisic acid also causes wilting of leaves.
keyPoints: Auxin and gibberellins or cytokinins promote growth
A second inhibitor such as ethylene
questions.explanation: Plant hormones coordinate growth and responses.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Bread mould (Rhizopus) reproduces by
questions.explanation: Rhizopus produces tiny spores in sporangia.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The ability of a Planaria to grow back lost body parts is called
questions.explanation: Specialised cells grow into the missing parts.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sexual reproduction gives more variation than asexual reproduction because
options: it happens only once in a lifetime
DNA from two different parents is combined
it does not involve DNA copying
questions.explanation: Mixing the genetic material of two parents gives new combinations.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The female reproductive part of a flower is the
questions.explanation: The pistil consists of stigma, style and ovary.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When a seed germinates, the part that develops into the root is the
questions.explanation: The radicle grows into the root and the plumule into the shoot.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In humans the testes lie outside the abdominal cavity in the scrotum because
options: sperm formation needs a temperature lower than the normal body temperature
questions.explanation: Sperm production needs a temperature slightly lower than body temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Define fertilisation.
questions.answer: Fertilisation is the fusion of a male gamete with a female gamete to form a zygote.
keyPoints: Fusion of male and female gametes
questions.explanation: The zygote develops into the embryo.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What happens to the thick lining of the uterus if the egg is not fertilised?
questions.answer: The uterus lining, which had thickened to receive the embryo, is not needed. It breaks down and passes out of the body with blood and mucus through the vagina as menstruation, about every month.
questions.explanation: The cycle repeats if no pregnancy occurs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Traits are passed from parents to offspring through units called
questions.explanation: Genes on chromosomes carry the information for traits.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A plant with round seeds (RR) is crossed with one with wrinkled seeds (rr) and the F1 plants are self-pollinated. The ratio of round to wrinkled seeds in F2 is
questions.explanation: Round is dominant, and F2 gives about 3 round to 1 wrinkled.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which statement about sex determination in humans is correct?
options: The sex of the child depends on whether an X-carrying or Y-carrying sperm fertilises the egg
The mother decides the sex because her eggs carry X or Y
The sex depends on the number of autosomes
The sex is decided after birth
questions.explanation: All eggs carry X, while sperm carry either X or Y.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The branch of biology that deals with heredity and variation is
questions.explanation: Genetics is the study of inheritance and variation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A pea plant has genotype Tt, where T is tall and t is dwarf. Its appearance is
questions.explanation: T is dominant, so Tt plants are tall.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A bodybuilder develops strong muscles by exercise, but his children are not born with strong muscles. This is because
options: muscles cannot be inherited by any means
acquired traits do not change the DNA of germ cells
questions.explanation: Only changes in the DNA of germ cells are inherited.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a gene?
questions.answer: A gene is a segment of DNA on a chromosome that carries the information for making a particular protein and controls a particular trait.
keyPoints: Segment of DNA on a chromosome
questions.explanation: Genes are the units of heredity.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Using a cross of a pure tall plant (TT) and a pure dwarf plant (tt), show how the dwarf trait reappears in the F2 generation.
questions.answer: The F1 plants are all Tt and tall. When F1 plants are self-pollinated they give TT, Tt, Tt and tt in F2, so one fourth are dwarf (tt) and the genotype ratio is 1:2:1.
keyPoints: F2 gives TT, Tt and tt
questions.explanation: The recessive allele is hidden in F1 and appears in tt plants.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The bending of light when it passes from one transparent medium to another is called
questions.explanation: The change in speed of light causes refraction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The image formed by a plane mirror is
options: virtual, erect and the same size as the object
questions.explanation: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect image equal in size to the object.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A lens forms an image with magnification -1. The image is
options: real, inverted and the same size as the object
virtual, erect and the same size
questions.explanation: A negative sign means the image is inverted and real, and a magnitude of 1 means same size.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A convex lens is also called a
questions.explanation: A convex lens converges parallel rays to a point.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The mirror formula is
questions.explanation: For a spherical mirror, 1/v + 1/u = 1/f.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An object is placed 10 cm from a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. The image is formed at
questions.explanation: An object at the focus gives refracted rays parallel to each other, so the image is at infinity.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Define the principal focus of a concave mirror.
questions.answer: The principal focus is the point on the principal axis where rays parallel to the axis meet after reflection from a concave mirror.
keyPoints: Rays parallel to the principal axis
Meet at a point after reflection
questions.explanation: The distance from the pole to this point is the focal length.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A ray of light goes from air into glass at an angle. Describe what happens to its path and why.
questions.answer: The ray bends towards the normal, because glass is optically denser and light travels more slowly in it than in air.
questions.explanation: Refraction occurs due to a change in the speed of light.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The image formed on the retina of a normal eye is
questions.explanation: The retina receives a real, inverted image, and the brain interprets it as upright.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: A person who cannot see nearby objects clearly (hypermetropia) is advised to use
questions.explanation: A convex lens converges the rays more so the image falls on the retina.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: In hypermetropia, the image of a nearby object is formed
questions.explanation: The eye lens is too weak or the eyeball too short, so the focus is behind the retina.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: A rainbow is formed in the sky mainly because of
options: reflection of light by clouds only
dispersion of sunlight by tiny water droplets
questions.explanation: Raindrops refract, disperse and internally reflect sunlight.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: Which colour of visible light bends the least on passing through a glass prism?
questions.explanation: Red has the longest wavelength and is deviated least.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: Danger signal lights are red because red light
options: is scattered the least by fog and smoke, so it can be seen from far away
is absorbed the most by air
questions.explanation: Red has the longest wavelength of visible light and is scattered least.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: What is cataract? How can it be treated?
questions.answer: In cataract the eye lens becomes cloudy or milky, causing partial or complete loss of vision. It can be treated by surgery to replace the lens with an artificial one.
questions.explanation: Cataract is common in old age.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: What is presbyopia and how is it corrected?
questions.answer: Presbyopia is a defect in old age in which the near point recedes and the person cannot see nearby objects clearly. It is corrected using bifocal lenses, with a concave upper part for distant vision and a convex lower part for near vision.
keyPoints: Near point moves away with age
Weakening of ciliary muscles and lens flexibility
questions.explanation: Accommodation power decreases with age.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of electrical resistance is
questions.explanation: Resistance is measured in ohms.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: If the current through a resistor is doubled, the heat produced in a given time becomes
questions.explanation: H = I squared x R x t, so doubling I gives four times the heat.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Three identical bulbs are connected in parallel to a battery and one of them fuses. What happens to the other two?
options: They continue to glow with the same brightness
questions.explanation: Each bulb has its own path with the full battery voltage across it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which device is used to measure the potential difference across a component?
questions.explanation: A voltmeter is connected in parallel with the component.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The electric power of an appliance is given by
questions.explanation: Power equals potential difference times current.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A 60 W bulb is connected to a 220 V supply. The current drawn is about
questions.explanation: I = P/V = 60/220, which is about 0.27 A.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Define potential difference between two points of a conductor.
questions.answer: The potential difference between two points is the work done to move a unit positive charge from one point to the other. Its SI unit is the volt.
questions.explanation: One volt is one joule per coulomb.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are household appliances connected in parallel and not in series?
questions.answer: In parallel each appliance gets the same full voltage and can be switched on or off independently. If one fails, the others keep working, and the total resistance is lower so enough current can flow.
keyPoints: Others keep working if one fails
questions.explanation: A series circuit would stop entirely if one appliance failed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Oersted's experiment showed that
options: an electric current produces a magnetic field
a magnet can produce an electric current
questions.explanation: A compass needle deflected near a current-carrying wire.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The magnetic field inside a long current-carrying solenoid is
questions.explanation: Inside a solenoid the field lines are parallel straight lines, showing a uniform field.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Soft iron is used as the core of an electromagnet because it
options: has a very high melting point
questions.explanation: Soft iron loses its magnetism when the current is switched off.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In India, the frequency of alternating current supplied to homes is
questions.explanation: AC in India reverses direction 100 times per second, a frequency of 50 Hz.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The metal body of an appliance is connected to the earth wire in order to
options: give a low-resistance path for leakage current and avoid shocks
questions.explanation: If the body becomes live, the current flows to the earth and the user is protected.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A 5 A fuse is fitted in a circuit and a current of 8 A flows through it. What is most likely to happen?
options: The fuse wire melts and breaks the circuit
The current falls to zero but the fuse is unaffected
questions.explanation: Excess current heats the low-melting-point wire so it melts, protecting the appliance.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State the right-hand thumb rule.
questions.answer: If you hold a current-carrying straight conductor in your right hand with the thumb pointing in the direction of the current, the fingers wrap around the conductor in the direction of the magnetic field.
keyPoints: Thumb shows the direction of current
Curled fingers show direction of field
questions.explanation: This gives the direction of the field around a straight wire.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is short-circuiting? When does it occur?
questions.answer: Short-circuiting is a very large current flowing in a circuit because of very low resistance. It occurs when the live and neutral wires touch each other, for instance when insulation is damaged.
questions.explanation: It can cause fires, so fuses are used.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these is a primary consumer?
questions.explanation: A grasshopper feeds on plants, so it is a herbivore.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a correct food chain?
questions.explanation: A food chain begins with a producer and the arrows show the direction of energy flow.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: If all the frogs in a pond ecosystem were removed, the number of insects on which they feed would most likely
questions.explanation: With the predator gone, the insects face less predation and their numbers rise.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The ozone layer protects living things from
questions.explanation: Ozone in the stratosphere absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet rays.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Ozone is formed in the upper atmosphere when ultraviolet radiation acts on
questions.explanation: UV splits O2 into atoms that combine with O2 to form O3.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which action will best reduce the waste problem in a town?
options: Burning all waste in the open
Separating waste and composting or recycling it
questions.explanation: Segregation allows composting of biodegradable waste and recycling of other materials.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is an ecosystem?
questions.answer: An ecosystem is a community of living organisms interacting with one another and with the non-living parts of their environment such as air, water and soil.
questions.explanation: Forests, ponds and gardens are examples.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is depletion of the ozone layer a matter of concern?
questions.answer: A thinner ozone layer allows more ultraviolet radiation to reach the Earth. This can cause skin cancer and cataract in humans and harm crops and other living things.
questions.explanation: Ozone absorbs harmful UV rays.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a chemical equation, the symbol (aq) written after a formula stands for
questions.explanation: (aq) means the substance is dissolved in water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A gas is released when zinc granules are treated with dilute sulphuric acid, and it burns with a pop sound near a flame. The gas is
questions.explanation: Hydrogen burns with a characteristic pop sound.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An iron nail kept in boiled distilled water with a layer of oil on top does not rust. This is because
options: oxygen is not available to the nail
water is not available to the nail
oil reacts with iron to protect it
questions.explanation: Boiling removes dissolved air and the oil stops air from dissolving again, and rusting needs both air and water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The chemical formula of lime water is
questions.explanation: Lime water is a solution of calcium hydroxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The gain of oxygen by a substance during a reaction is called
questions.explanation: Oxidation is gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the reaction CuO + H2 giving Cu + H2O, the oxidising agent is
questions.explanation: CuO gives its oxygen to hydrogen, so it oxidises hydrogen and is itself reduced.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write the balanced chemical equation for the burning of magnesium in air.
questions.answer: 2Mg + O2 gives 2MgO. Magnesium combines with oxygen to form magnesium oxide, with the release of a dazzling white flame.
questions.explanation: There are two Mg atoms and two O atoms on each side.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are iron objects painted, greased or galvanised?
questions.answer: These coatings keep air and moisture away from the iron and so prevent rusting. In galvanisation the iron is coated with a layer of zinc, which protects it.
keyPoints: Stops contact with air and moisture
questions.explanation: Rusting needs both oxygen and water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A solution of pH 3 will
questions.explanation: A pH below 7 means the solution is acidic, and acids turn blue litmus red.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The reaction between an acid and a base produces
questions.explanation: This neutralisation reaction gives a salt and water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Using a slightly basic toothpaste helps prevent tooth decay because it
options: adds more acid to the mouth
neutralises the acid produced by bacteria in the mouth
questions.explanation: Bacteria produce acid from leftover sugar, and the base neutralises it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Sodium hydroxide is commonly known as
questions.explanation: NaOH is called caustic soda.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is manufactured using common salt as a raw material?
questions.explanation: Washing soda is made from sodium chloride via sodium carbonate.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: On adding a substance to a solution its pH rises from 4 to 9. The substance added is most likely
questions.explanation: Adding a base makes a solution less acidic and then basic, raising pH.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Write two uses of baking soda.
questions.answer: It is used in baking powder to make cakes and bread rise, and as an antacid to reduce acidity in the stomach. It is also used in soda-acid fire extinguishers.
questions.explanation: Its mild basic nature and release of CO2 make it useful.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why should concentrated acid be added slowly to water and not water to the acid when diluting?
questions.answer: Dissolving an acid in water is highly exothermic. Adding acid slowly to water lets the heat spread through the water, but adding water to acid can make the mixture splash out because of the local heat.
keyPoints: Slow addition to water spreads the heat
Reverse order may cause splashing and burns
questions.explanation: This is a standard laboratory safety practice.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is the best conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Silver is the best conductor, followed by copper.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is an amphoteric oxide?
questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide reacts with both acids and bases.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Aqua regia, which can dissolve gold, is a mixture of
options: concentrated HCl and concentrated H2SO4 in a 1:3 ratio
concentrated HCl and concentrated HNO3 in a 3:1 ratio
dilute HCl and dilute HNO3 in a 1:1 ratio
concentrated H2SO4 and concentrated HNO3 in a 3:1 ratio
questions.explanation: Aqua regia is 3 parts concentrated HCl to 1 part concentrated HNO3.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Coating iron with a layer of zinc to prevent rusting is called
questions.explanation: Galvanisation protects iron by a zinc coat.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Roasting is a process in which the ore is heated
questions.explanation: Sulphide ores are roasted in excess of air to give oxides.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Highly reactive metals such as sodium are extracted by
questions.explanation: Their oxides cannot easily be reduced by carbon, so electrolysis is used.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two physical properties of metals.
questions.answer: Metals are generally lustrous, hard, malleable and ductile, and they are good conductors of heat and electricity. They usually have high melting points.
keyPoints: Any one correct property such as malleability or ductility
A second correct property such as conductivity or lustre
questions.explanation: These properties distinguish metals from most non-metals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe how zinc is obtained from its sulphide ore, zinc blende.
questions.answer: Zinc blende is first roasted in air to form zinc oxide and sulphur dioxide. Zinc oxide is then reduced to zinc by heating with carbon.
keyPoints: Roasting converts the sulphide to oxide
Carbon reduces zinc oxide to zinc
questions.explanation: Moderately reactive metals are extracted by reduction with carbon.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The main constituent of natural gas (CNG) is
questions.explanation: Natural gas is mostly methane.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the hydrogenation of vegetable oils, which catalyst is used?
questions.explanation: Unsaturated vegetable oils are converted to saturated fats by hydrogen with nickel as catalyst.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Soap does not lather well in hard water and forms a scum because
options: calcium and magnesium salts in hard water react with soap to form an insoluble scum
questions.explanation: The scum is an insoluble calcium or magnesium salt of the fatty acid.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures are called
questions.explanation: For example, butane and isobutane are isomers.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The reaction of an ester with sodium hydroxide to form soap is called
questions.explanation: Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of fats or esters.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Carbon forms a very large number of compounds mainly because
options: carbon forms long chains and has a valency of four
questions.explanation: Catenation and tetravalency allow many different structures.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What products are formed when ethanol burns in sufficient air?
questions.answer: Ethanol burns in air to give carbon dioxide and water along with heat and light.
questions.explanation: This is complete combustion of an organic fuel.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the role of concentrated sulphuric acid when ethanol is heated at 443 K with excess of it to form ethene?
questions.answer: Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent. It removes a molecule of water from ethanol, giving ethene.
questions.explanation: Ethanol loses water in this dehydration reaction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The gas released as a by-product during photosynthesis is
questions.explanation: Oxygen is released when water is split during photosynthesis.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The enzyme pepsin in the stomach works best in a medium that is
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid in the stomach provides the acidic medium for pepsin.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Veins in the legs have valves because
options: the blood there carries more oxygen
the walls of veins are thin
the blood is pumped out of the heart through them
blood flows at low pressure and the valves keep it moving only towards the heart
questions.explanation: Valves prevent backflow of blood in the veins.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to the tissues?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin that carries oxygen.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Plants lose water vapour to the air mainly through
questions.explanation: Loss of water vapour through stomata is called transpiration.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In tall trees, water rises from the roots to the leaves mainly because of
options: suction created by transpiration from the leaves
questions.explanation: Water evaporating from leaves pulls a column of water up the xylem.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is transpiration?
questions.answer: Transpiration is the loss of water in the form of vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mainly through the stomata of leaves.
questions.explanation: It helps water movement and cools the plant.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Differentiate between the functions of xylem and phloem.
questions.answer: Xylem carries water and minerals from the roots to the other parts of the plant. Phloem transports food, such as the sugars made in leaves, to the other parts of the plant, in both directions.
keyPoints: Phloem carries food made in leaves
questions.explanation: Together they form the transport system in plants.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The largest and most complex part of the human brain is the
questions.explanation: The cerebrum is responsible for thinking, memory and voluntary actions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a voluntary action?
questions.explanation: Writing is under conscious control of the cerebrum.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A person whose diet lacks iodine may develop a swollen neck (goitre) because
options: the thyroid cannot make enough thyroxine and enlarges
the pancreas makes too much insulin
the pituitary stops making growth hormone
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed for thyroxine, and lack of it causes the thyroid gland to swell.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A nerve cell is also called a
questions.explanation: The neuron is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Diabetes is caused mainly by
questions.explanation: Without enough insulin, blood sugar stays high.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When a person is suddenly frightened, adrenaline released into the blood causes
options: a faster heartbeat and more blood flow to the muscles
questions.explanation: Adrenaline prepares the body for fight or flight.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name the gland that secretes thyroxine and state one function of the hormone.
questions.answer: The thyroid gland secretes thyroxine, which regulates the metabolism of carbohydrates, fats and proteins in the body.
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed to make thyroxine.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How do the leaves of the touch-me-not (Mimosa) plant droop when touched?
questions.answer: On touch, the plant sends signals from cell to cell, and the cells in the leaf joints quickly lose water. They shrink and the leaves fold and droop. This is a change in cell size, not growth.
questions.explanation: This is different from tropic movements, which are growth based.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Reproduction in which new individuals arise from a single parent without the fusion of gametes is called
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction involves one parent only.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Rose and sugarcane can be grown from stem cuttings. This is an example of
questions.explanation: New plants grow from vegetative parts of the old plant.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A complex organism such as a human cannot reproduce by cutting its body into pieces because
options: humans have no cells that divide
the body is highly organised with specialised cells and organs that cannot regrow a whole individual
questions.explanation: Complex organisms have cells organised into tissues and organs, so they cannot simply regenerate the whole body from fragments.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The fusion of a male gamete with a female gamete gives a
questions.explanation: The fertilised egg is called a zygote.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: After fertilisation in a flower, the ovary develops into a
questions.explanation: The ovules become seeds and the ovary becomes the fruit.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Pollen from the anther of one flower is carried to the stigma of a flower on a different plant of the same species. This is called
questions.explanation: Pollination between flowers of different plants is cross-pollination.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name the male and the female gametes in humans.
questions.answer: The male gamete is the sperm, produced in the testes, and the female gamete is the egg (ovum), produced in the ovaries.
keyPoints: Egg or ovum is female gamete
questions.explanation: Fertilisation is the fusion of these two.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two changes seen in boys and two changes seen in girls at puberty.
questions.answer: In boys, the voice deepens and facial hair (a beard or moustache) grows. In girls, the breasts develop and menstruation begins. In both, hair grows in the armpits and genital area.
questions.explanation: Hormones trigger these changes at puberty.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Chromosomes are mainly made of
questions.explanation: Chromosomes contain DNA wrapped with proteins.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The number of chromosomes in a normal human sperm cell is
questions.explanation: Gametes carry half of the 46 chromosomes of a body cell.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A tall pea plant of genotype Tt is crossed with a dwarf plant tt. What fraction of the offspring is expected to be dwarf?
questions.explanation: Tt x tt gives Tt and tt in equal numbers, so half the offspring are dwarf.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A characteristic of an organism, such as the colour of its flowers, is called a
questions.explanation: A trait is an observable feature.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which cross will give only dwarf pea plants in the offspring?
questions.explanation: Both parents can pass on only the recessive allele t.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Brothers and sisters from the same parents often look different from each other because
options: each gamete carries a different random mix of chromosomes from the parent
questions.explanation: Random assortment and fusion of gametes gives different gene combinations.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What are autosomes and sex chromosomes in humans?
questions.answer: Humans have 22 pairs of autosomes, which carry genes for body traits, and one pair of sex chromosomes that decides the sex of the person: XX in females and XY in males.
questions.explanation: In all, a human has 23 pairs of chromosomes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain how the sex of a child is determined in humans.
questions.answer: A woman has XX chromosomes, so every egg carries an X. A man has XY, so half the sperm carry X and half carry Y. If a sperm with X fertilises the egg the child is a girl, and if a sperm with Y does, the child is a boy.
keyPoints: X gives a girl and Y gives a boy
questions.explanation: The father's sperm decides the sex of the child.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The centre of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is called its
questions.explanation: The pole is the geometric centre of the mirror surface.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The refractive index of glass is 1.5 and the speed of light in vacuum is 3 x 10^8 m/s. The speed of light in glass is

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A convex mirror always forms an image that is
questions.explanation: Whatever the position of the object, a convex mirror gives a virtual, erect, smaller image.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A ray of light passing through the optical centre of a lens
questions.explanation: Rays through the optical centre emerge in the same direction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A concave mirror forms a virtual, erect and magnified image when the object is placed
options: between the pole and the focus
questions.explanation: Only within the focal length does a concave mirror give a magnified virtual image.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A student gets a sharp image of a distant tree on a screen using a concave mirror. The mirror-to-screen distance is 20 cm. The focal length of the mirror is about
questions.explanation: Rays from a distant object are nearly parallel, so the image forms at the focus.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State Snell's law of refraction.
questions.answer: For light going from one medium to another, the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant for a given pair of media.
keyPoints: Ratio of sin i to sin r
questions.explanation: The constant is the refractive index of the second medium with respect to the first.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A pencil partly dipped in water in a glass appears bent at the water surface. Explain.
questions.answer: Light from the part of the pencil in water bends away from the normal as it passes into air, because light travels faster in air than in water. This refraction makes the submerged part appear to be at a different position, so the pencil looks bent.
keyPoints: Apparent shift of the submerged part
questions.explanation: The effect is caused by refraction.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The transparent front part of the eye is called the
questions.explanation: Most refraction of light entering the eye takes place at the cornea.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The focal length of the eye lens is adjusted by the
questions.explanation: Ciliary muscles change the curvature of the lens.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The far point of a normal human eye is
questions.explanation: A normal eye can see very distant objects such as stars clearly.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: Among the colours of the spectrum, the one with the shortest wavelength is
questions.explanation: Violet has the shortest wavelength and red the longest.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The Tyndall effect can be seen when a beam of light passes through
options: air filled with fine smoke or dust
questions.explanation: Fine particles scatter the light and make the path of the beam visible.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: We see the Sun a couple of minutes before it actually rises above the horizon because of
questions.explanation: The atmosphere bends sunlight so the Sun appears raised.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: What is the Tyndall effect?
questions.answer: The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal or very fine particles in a medium, which makes the path of a beam of light visible. It is seen when sunlight enters a dense forest through the mist.
keyPoints: Scattering of light by fine particles
Path of the beam becomes visible
questions.explanation: The effect is named after John Tyndall.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: Why does the sky appear dark to astronauts in space, though it appears blue from the ground?
questions.answer: In space there is no atmosphere to scatter sunlight, so no light is scattered towards the astronaut's eyes and the sky looks dark. On Earth the air molecules scatter blue light, giving a blue sky.
keyPoints: Scattering by air on Earth gives blue
questions.explanation: The blue sky is an effect of scattering in the atmosphere.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The rate of flow of electric charge is called
questions.explanation: Current equals charge flowing per second.

questions.subject: science
