questions.q: Resistors of 3 ohm and 6 ohm are connected in series. The equivalent resistance is
questions.explanation: In series, resistances add up: 3 + 6 = 9 ohm.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A 6 ohm and a 12 ohm resistor are connected in parallel across a 12 V battery. The total current drawn from the battery is
questions.explanation: The currents are 12/6 = 2 A and 12/12 = 1 A, so the total is 3 A.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is an electrical insulator?
questions.explanation: Rubber has very high resistivity.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The SI unit of resistivity of a material is
questions.explanation: Resistivity = RA/L, which has the unit ohm metre.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: One kilowatt-hour is equal to

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State the factors on which the resistance of a conductor depends.
questions.answer: The resistance depends on the length of the conductor (directly), its area of cross-section (inversely), the material it is made of, and its temperature.
questions.explanation: R = rho x L / A for a given material.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is the heating effect of electric current? Give two applications.
questions.answer: When current flows through a resistor, electrical energy is converted into heat. This is used in electric heaters, irons and toasters, and in the filament of electric bulbs, and in a fuse.
questions.explanation: Heat produced is I squared x R x t.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which device is used to detect the presence of current in a circuit?
questions.explanation: A galvanometer shows deflection when a current is present.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An AC generator produces
questions.explanation: A coil rotating in a magnetic field produces current that reverses direction periodically.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The force on a current-carrying conductor placed parallel to a magnetic field is
questions.explanation: The force is maximum when the conductor is perpendicular to the field and zero when it is parallel.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The magnetic field of a bar magnet is strongest near its
questions.explanation: Field lines are closest together near the poles.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following gives direct current?
questions.explanation: A cell or battery gives a current that flows in one direction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How can the direction of rotation of the coil of a DC motor be reversed?
options: By reversing the direction of the current
questions.explanation: Reversing the current reverses the force, so the coil turns the other way.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is an electromagnet?
questions.answer: An electromagnet is a strong magnet made by winding insulated wire into a coil around a soft iron core and passing an electric current through it. It works as a magnet only while the current flows.
keyPoints: Coil of wire around a soft iron core
questions.explanation: Electromagnets are used in cranes and electric bells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain the working principle of an electric generator.
questions.answer: A generator works on electromagnetic induction. When the coil is rotated in a magnetic field, the magnetic field through it keeps changing, which induces a current in the coil, so mechanical energy is changed into electrical energy.
keyPoints: Coil rotates in a magnetic field
questions.explanation: The changing flux induces the current.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is non-biodegradable?
questions.explanation: Microorganisms cannot break down most plastics.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the food chain grass, grasshopper, frog, snake, the secondary consumer is the
questions.explanation: The frog feeds on the grasshopper, which is the primary consumer.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the food chain plants, insects, fish, fish-eating birds, a non-biodegradable pesticide will be found in the highest concentration in
questions.explanation: The pesticide accumulates at each level, so it is highest at the top trophic level.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is an abiotic component of an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Abiotic components are the non-living parts.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Each step of a food chain is called a
questions.explanation: Producers, herbivores and carnivores occupy different trophic levels.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A food web is generally more stable than a single food chain because
options: organisms have alternative sources of food
questions.explanation: If one food source declines, consumers can switch to another.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a food web?
questions.answer: A food web is a network of many interconnected food chains in an ecosystem, showing the different feeding relationships between organisms.
questions.explanation: Most organisms eat or are eaten by more than one kind of organism.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How does the disposal of plastic waste harm the environment?
questions.answer: Plastic is non-biodegradable, so it stays for a very long time. It chokes drains, can be swallowed by animals which fall ill, and burning it gives off poisonous gases.
questions.explanation: Reducing and recycling plastic helps the environment.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a combination reaction?
questions.explanation: Two substances, carbon and oxygen, combine to form a single product.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Potassium iodide solution is added to lead nitrate solution. The precipitate formed has the colour
questions.explanation: Lead iodide, a yellow solid, is formed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the balanced equation CH4 + xO2 giving CO2 + 2H2O, the value of x is
questions.explanation: There are four oxygen atoms on the right (two in CO2 and two in 2H2O), so two O2 molecules are needed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a chemical reaction, the substances that undergo change are called
questions.explanation: Reactants are written on the left-hand side of an equation.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is an endothermic process?
options: Decomposition of calcium carbonate by heating
questions.explanation: Heat has to be supplied continuously to decompose calcium carbonate.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A burnt magnesium ribbon leaves white ash that weighs more than the original ribbon. This is because
options: oxygen from the air combined with the magnesium
mass is created in a chemical reaction
questions.explanation: The ash is magnesium oxide, which contains the added mass of oxygen.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a precipitation reaction? Give an example.
questions.answer: A precipitation reaction is one in which an insoluble solid, called a precipitate, is formed when two solutions are mixed. For example, sodium sulphate and barium chloride solutions give white barium sulphate.
keyPoints: An insoluble solid forms from solutions
questions.explanation: The solid that settles is the precipitate.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Decomposition reactions can be brought about by heat, light or electricity. Give one example for each.
questions.answer: By heat: calcium carbonate giving calcium oxide and carbon dioxide. By light: silver chloride giving silver and chlorine. By electricity: water giving hydrogen and oxygen on electrolysis.
questions.explanation: Each form of energy breaks a compound into simpler substances.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The sour taste of lemon juice is due to the presence of
questions.explanation: Citrus fruits contain citric acid.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The acid secreted in the human stomach is
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid helps digestion and kills germs in the stomach.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following solutions has the highest concentration of hydroxide ions?
questions.explanation: The higher the pH above 7, the more basic the solution.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: When a metal reacts with a dilute acid, a salt and which gas are formed?
questions.explanation: Metals displace hydrogen from acids.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Bleaching powder is used for
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is used to disinfect water and as a bleaching agent.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Blue crystals of copper sulphate turn white on strong heating. This is because the crystals
questions.explanation: The blue colour is due to 5 molecules of water of crystallisation, which are lost on heating.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a neutralisation reaction? Give an example.
questions.answer: A neutralisation reaction is the reaction of an acid with a base to give a salt and water. For example, HCl + NaOH gives NaCl + H2O.
questions.explanation: The effects of the acid and the base cancel.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is water of crystallisation? Give two examples of salts that have it.
questions.answer: It is the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt in crystal form. Examples are CuSO4.5H2O (blue vitriol) and Na2CO3.10H2O (washing soda); gypsum is another.
keyPoints: Fixed number of water molecules in the crystal
questions.explanation: Loss of this water often changes the colour of the crystals.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The most abundant metal in the Earth's crust is
questions.explanation: Aluminium is the most abundant metal in the crust.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these metals does not react with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Metal P displaces metal Q from its salt solution, and metal Q displaces metal R from its salt solution. The order from most to least reactive is
questions.explanation: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one, so P is above Q and Q is above R.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which metal is found in the free state in nature?
questions.explanation: Gold is so unreactive that it occurs native.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Oxides of non-metals are generally
questions.explanation: Non-metal oxides such as CO2 and SO2 dissolve in water to give acids.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Copper rather than silver is used for most electrical wires mainly because
options: copper is much cheaper and still a very good conductor
questions.explanation: Silver is a slightly better conductor, but its cost is far higher.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What are amphoteric oxides? Give an example.
questions.answer: Amphoteric oxides are metal oxides that react with both acids and bases to give salt and water. Examples are aluminium oxide and zinc oxide.
keyPoints: React with both acids and bases
Example such as Al2O3 or ZnO
questions.explanation: They show both acidic and basic behaviour.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: List three properties of ionic compounds.
questions.answer: They are hard, brittle solids with high melting and boiling points. They are generally soluble in water but not in kerosene, and they conduct electricity in the molten state or in solution but not as solids.
keyPoints: Hard solids with high melting points
Conduct when molten or in solution
questions.explanation: These follow from the strong force between ions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The compound with the formula CH3OH is called
questions.explanation: CH3OH has an -OH group on a one-carbon chain, so it is methanol.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The molecular formula of butane is
questions.explanation: Butane is an alkane with four carbons, CnH(2n+2) = C4H10.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a soap micelle in water, the ionic ends of the soap molecules point
options: towards the centre where the tails are
questions.explanation: The hydrocarbon tails gather inside with the oil, and the ionic heads face the surrounding water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The functional group -CHO is present in
questions.explanation: -CHO is the aldehyde group.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: C2H6 (ethane) has only single bonds.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Graphite is used as a lubricant because
options: its atoms are held by ionic bonds
its layers of carbon atoms are held together weakly and can slide over each other
questions.explanation: Weak forces between layers let them slip easily.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name two allotropes of carbon.
questions.answer: Diamond and graphite are two allotropes of carbon. Fullerene (such as C-60) is another.
questions.explanation: Allotropes are different forms of the same element.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does carbon form compounds by sharing electrons and not by forming ions?
questions.answer: Carbon has four electrons in its outer shell. Gaining four electrons would need too much energy for the nucleus to hold, and losing four electrons would also need a huge amount of energy. So carbon shares electrons and forms covalent bonds.
keyPoints: Gaining or losing four electrons is hard
questions.explanation: Sharing gives carbon a stable electronic arrangement.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which part of a plant absorbs water from the soil?
questions.explanation: Root hairs have a large surface area for absorption.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The chamber of the human heart that has the thickest wall and pumps oxygenated blood to the whole body is the
questions.explanation: The left ventricle must push blood through the whole body, so it has a thick muscular wall.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood even though it is an artery, because
options: arteries are defined as vessels carrying blood away from the heart, and this one goes to the lungs
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, whether oxygen-rich or oxygen-poor.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The digestion of proteins begins in the
questions.explanation: Pepsin in the stomach starts to break down proteins.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Peristalsis is
options: the movement of food along the alimentary canal by contraction of its walls
questions.explanation: Rhythmic contraction pushes food forward through the canal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A leaf kept in the dark for 24 hours does not show starch when tested with iodine. This is because
options: iodine does not react with starch
photosynthesis cannot take place without light and the stored starch has been used
questions.explanation: Without light no new starch is made, and the old starch is consumed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State the role of saliva in digestion.
questions.answer: Saliva moistens the food and makes it easy to swallow. The enzyme salivary amylase in it begins breaking down starch into sugar.
questions.explanation: Digestion begins in the mouth.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe in brief how urine is formed in the kidney.
questions.answer: Blood is filtered in the glomerulus of the nephron, and the filtrate enters the tubule. Useful substances such as glucose and water are reabsorbed into the blood, and the remaining liquid with urea is urine, which is collected and sent to the bladder.
questions.explanation: Nephrons filter and clean the blood.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which organ detects smell?
questions.explanation: Olfactory receptors in the nose detect smells.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The part of a neuron that carries the impulse away from the cell body is the
questions.explanation: The axon passes the impulse on to other neurons or to muscles.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which part of the brain controls involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation and vomiting?
questions.explanation: The medulla in the hindbrain controls many involuntary functions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The brain is protected inside the
questions.explanation: The bony box of the skull protects the brain.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The male sex hormone testosterone is secreted by the
questions.explanation: Testosterone from the testes brings the changes of puberty in boys.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The tip of a shoot is covered with an opaque cap and light is given from one side. The shoot does not bend towards the light. The most likely reason is that
options: the cap makes the plant too hot
light is not sensed at the tip, where auxin is made, so auxin is not redistributed
the cap stops photosynthesis in the whole plant
questions.explanation: Auxin is made at the tip, and light-driven shifting of auxin to the shaded side causes bending.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two functions of the cerebrum.
questions.answer: The cerebrum is the centre of thinking, memory and learning. It controls voluntary actions and receives and interprets information from the sense organs.
questions.explanation: It is the largest part of the brain.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Explain the feedback mechanism that controls the blood sugar level.
questions.answer: When blood sugar rises, the pancreas secretes more insulin, which helps the body use or store the sugar and the level falls. When it falls, insulin secretion is reduced, so the level stays within a normal range.
keyPoints: Rise in sugar leads to more insulin
Less insulin when sugar is low
questions.explanation: Hormone release is regulated by the effect it produces.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following reproduces by fragmentation?
questions.explanation: A Spirogyra filament breaks into pieces that grow into new filaments.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Yeast reproduces asexually mainly by
questions.explanation: A small bud grows out of the yeast cell and separates.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Banana plants are grown by vegetative propagation rather than from seeds because
options: they produce far too many seeds
they do not produce viable seeds
questions.explanation: Cultivated bananas are seedless, so new plants come from suckers.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Pollen grains are produced in the
questions.explanation: The anther is the part of the stamen that makes pollen.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In a human female, an egg is normally released from an ovary about once in
questions.explanation: One egg is released roughly every month.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which contraceptive method also helps protect against sexually transmitted infections?
questions.explanation: A condom is a barrier that prevents contact of body fluids.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is vegetative propagation? Give two examples of plants grown this way.
questions.answer: It is a type of asexual reproduction in which new plants grow from vegetative parts such as the root, stem or leaf. Rose and sugarcane (stem cutting), potato (tuber), and Bryophyllum (leaf) are examples.
keyPoints: New plants from roots, stems or leaves
questions.explanation: No seeds or gametes are involved.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two advantages of vegetative propagation.
questions.answer: Plants that do not produce viable seeds, such as banana and jasmine, can be grown. The new plants are genetically identical to the parent and often bear flowers and fruits earlier than those grown from seeds.
questions.explanation: Growers use it to keep good qualities.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The chemical that carries genetic information in most organisms is
questions.explanation: DNA is the hereditary material in most living things.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A pure round yellow-seeded pea plant is crossed with a pure wrinkled green-seeded plant. All the F1 plants have
questions.explanation: Round and yellow are the dominant traits.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the F2 generation of a dihybrid cross between round yellow (RRYY) and wrinkled green (rryy) pea plants, what fraction of plants have round green seeds?
questions.explanation: The 9:3:3:1 ratio has 9 round yellow, 3 round green, 3 wrinkled yellow and 1 wrinkled green.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Gregor Mendel did his experiments on
questions.explanation: He studied the inheritance of seven contrasting traits of the garden pea.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A trait that is not expressed in the presence of its contrasting trait is
questions.explanation: Recessive traits show up only when no dominant allele is present.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A man's Y chromosome is passed on to
questions.explanation: Only sons receive a Y chromosome, and daughters receive his X.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a monohybrid cross?
questions.answer: A monohybrid cross is a cross between two parents that differ in a single pair of contrasting traits, for example a tall plant and a dwarf plant.
keyPoints: Differing in one pair of contrasting traits
questions.explanation: It gives a 3:1 ratio in F2.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Differentiate between inherited traits and acquired traits with one example each.
questions.answer: Inherited traits are passed from parents through genes in the germ cells, such as eye colour. Acquired traits are gained during a person's life, such as a skill learned or a scar, and are not passed on to the next generation.
questions.explanation: Only changes in germ cell DNA are inherited.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The distance between the pole of a mirror and its principal focus is called
questions.explanation: That distance is the focal length.

questions.q: The power of a lens of focal length 0.5 m is

questions.q: A 5 cm tall object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. The image is
options: 30 cm in front of the mirror, 5 cm tall and inverted
15 cm behind the mirror, 2.5 cm tall and erect
30 cm behind the mirror, 5 cm tall and erect
15 cm in front of the mirror, 10 cm tall and inverted
questions.explanation: The object is at the centre of curvature (2f), so the image is at the same place, same size and inverted.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which lens is thicker in the middle than at the edges?
questions.explanation: A convex lens bulges outward in the middle.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A ray of light that passes through the principal focus of a concave mirror, after reflection, moves
questions.explanation: By the reversibility of light, a ray through the focus becomes parallel to the axis.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A ray of light goes obliquely from glass into air. In air it
questions.explanation: Going from a denser to a rarer medium, light speeds up and bends away from the normal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Define 1 dioptre.
questions.answer: One dioptre is the power of a lens whose focal length is 1 metre.
keyPoints: Unit of power of a lens
questions.explanation: P = 1/f with f in metres.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Describe the image formed by a convex lens when the object is placed between its focus and optical centre. State one use of this.
questions.answer: The image is virtual, erect and magnified, and is formed on the same side of the lens as the object. This is how a magnifying glass works.
questions.explanation: The lens is held close to the object.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye is the
questions.explanation: The retina has cells that respond to light and send signals to the brain.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: At noon the Sun appears white (not red) because
options: light travels a shorter path through the atmosphere, so less blue is scattered away
questions.explanation: With a shorter path, only a little of the blue light is scattered out of the beam.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: A person cannot see distant objects clearly beyond about 2 m. The defect and the correcting lens are
questions.explanation: This is short-sightedness, which is corrected by a diverging (concave) lens.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The light-sensitive cells in the retina are
questions.explanation: Rods respond to dim light and cones to bright light and colour.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The lens of the human eye is a
questions.explanation: It is a convex lens that focuses an image on the retina.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: After walking into a dim room from bright sunlight, we cannot see clearly for a short time. This is because
options: the pupil takes time to enlarge and let in more light
questions.explanation: The iris muscles take a little time to widen the pupil.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: What are the functions of the iris and the pupil?
questions.answer: The pupil is the opening through which light enters the eye. The iris is a muscular diaphragm that changes the size of the pupil to control the amount of light entering.
keyPoints: Iris controls the size of pupil
questions.explanation: The pupil gets smaller in bright light.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: How do rod cells and cone cells in the retina differ in function?
questions.answer: Rod cells respond to dim light and help in seeing at night. Cone cells respond to bright light and detect colours.
keyPoints: Cones work in bright light and detect colour
questions.explanation: Together they let us see in different conditions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An ammeter is always connected to a circuit in
questions.explanation: The ammeter must carry the full circuit current.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A current of 2 A flows through a wire for 5 seconds. The charge that flows is
questions.explanation: Q = I x t = 2 x 5 = 10 C.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Two wires A and B are made of the same material and have equal lengths. Wire A has twice the cross-sectional area of B. The ratio of resistance R_A to R_B is
questions.explanation: Resistance is inversely proportional to the area, so A has half the resistance of B.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The magnitude of the charge on one electron is about
questions.explanation: The elementary charge is 1.6 x 10^-19 coulomb.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A 6 V battery is connected across a 3 ohm resistor. The current is

questions.subject: science

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What does a power of 1 watt mean?
questions.answer: One watt is the power of a device that uses or converts one joule of energy in one second.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why is nichrome used in heating elements while copper is used for connecting wires?
questions.answer: Nichrome has a high resistivity and a high melting point and does not oxidise easily at high temperatures, so it heats up well. Copper has very low resistivity, so it carries current with little loss of heat.
keyPoints: Nichrome has high resistivity and melting point
questions.explanation: The choice depends on whether heat is wanted or not.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Two magnetic field lines never
options: go from the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet
questions.explanation: If they crossed there would be two directions of the field at one point.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The magnetic field produced by a straight current-carrying wire at a point becomes stronger when
options: the distance from the wire increases
the wire is made of copper
questions.explanation: The field is proportional to the current and falls with distance.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The number of turns in a circular coil is doubled while the current stays the same. The magnetic field at its centre
questions.explanation: Each turn adds its own field, so the field is proportional to the number of turns.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A magnetic compass needle is
questions.explanation: It is a tiny magnet that aligns with the Earth's magnetic field.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: India's AC supply reverses its direction after every
questions.explanation: At 50 Hz, the current reverses 100 times in a second, which is every 1/100 s.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of these will increase the current induced in a coil when a magnet is moved into it?
options: Using a coil with fewer turns
questions.explanation: A faster change in the magnetic field induces a larger current.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State Fleming's left-hand rule.
questions.answer: Stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand at right angles to one another. If the forefinger points along the magnetic field and the middle finger along the current, the thumb gives the direction of force on the conductor.
questions.explanation: It gives the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is overloading in a domestic electric circuit and when does it occur?
questions.answer: Overloading is the flow of more current than the circuit is designed to carry. It occurs when too many appliances are connected to a single socket, or when the supply voltage suddenly rises.
keyPoints: Too many appliances on a socket
questions.explanation: A fuse protects against overloading.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which organisms form the first trophic level in a food chain?
questions.explanation: Producers are green plants that capture the Sun's energy.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which organisms are called the natural cleaners of the environment?
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down dead matter and wastes.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: If the producers in a food chain fix 10000 J of energy, about how much energy reaches the tertiary consumers (using the 10 percent law)?
questions.explanation: Producers 10000, primary 1000, secondary 100, tertiary 10 J.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: CFCs were widely used in
questions.explanation: CFCs were used as coolants and propellants until they were found to harm the ozone layer.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is a man-made ecosystem?
questions.explanation: A crop field is created and maintained by people.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which habit would best reduce non-biodegradable waste?
questions.explanation: Reusable cloth bags reduce the use of plastic.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What are producers? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Producers are organisms that make their own food by photosynthesis, using sunlight. Green plants and algae are examples.
keyPoints: Two examples such as plants and algae
questions.explanation: All other organisms depend on producers for food.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What happens to the amount of energy as it moves along a food chain? Why?
questions.answer: The amount of energy decreases at each step, with only about 10 percent passing to the next trophic level. The rest is lost as heat or used up in the organism's life processes such as respiration.
keyPoints: The rest is lost as heat or used by the organism
questions.explanation: This is why food chains are short.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting forms a new substance, iron oxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which gas is released when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to sodium carbonate?
questions.explanation: Carbonates react with acids to give a salt, water and carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Copper powder is heated in air in a china dish and it turns black. The black substance is
questions.explanation: Copper combines with oxygen to form black copper(II) oxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The reaction between an acid and a base to form salt and water is called
questions.explanation: This is a neutralisation reaction.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the reaction Zn + H2SO4 giving ZnSO4 + H2, which statement is correct?
options: It is a double displacement reaction
Zinc displaces hydrogen from the acid
questions.explanation: A more reactive metal displaces hydrogen from the acid.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In the balanced equation C2H5OH + 3O2 giving 2CO2 + yH2O, the value of y is
questions.explanation: Ethanol has 6 hydrogen atoms, so 3 water molecules are needed.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a redox reaction?
questions.answer: A redox reaction is a reaction in which oxidation and reduction take place at the same time: one substance is oxidised while another is reduced.
keyPoints: One substance oxidised and another reduced
questions.explanation: For example, CuO + H2 gives Cu + H2O.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does a copper vessel lose its shine and get a green coating when left in moist air?
questions.answer: Copper reacts slowly with moisture, carbon dioxide and oxygen in the air. This forms a green coating of basic copper carbonate, which is an example of corrosion.
questions.explanation: The metal is attacked by substances in the air.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which indicator turns pink in a basic solution?
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acids and pink in bases.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Milk of magnesia, used as an antacid, contains
questions.explanation: Magnesium hydroxide is a mild base that neutralises stomach acid.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A bee sting injects formic acid. Which of these can be rubbed on the sting to give relief?
questions.explanation: A mild base neutralises the acid, whereas the others are acidic.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The chemical formula of sulphuric acid is
questions.explanation: Sulphuric acid contains two hydrogen, one sulphur and four oxygen atoms.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Acid solutions conduct electricity because they contain
questions.explanation: Acids form H+ ions and other ions in water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A milkman adds a little baking soda to fresh milk, and the milk takes longer to set as curd. The reason is that
options: the milk becomes slightly alkaline, so more acid must be produced to set it
baking soda kills all the bacteria
baking soda turns milk into water
questions.explanation: Baking soda raises the pH, and curd forms only after enough acid is produced.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Name the products formed when an acid reacts with a metal carbonate.
questions.answer: A salt, water and carbon dioxide gas are formed.
questions.explanation: For example, Na2CO3 + 2HCl gives 2NaCl + H2O + CO2.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why does an aqueous solution of an acid conduct electricity while a glucose solution does not?
questions.answer: Acids split into ions (such as H+) in water, and these moving ions carry current. Glucose contains hydrogen but does not form ions in water, so its solution does not conduct.
questions.explanation: Conduction needs free ions.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is the most malleable metal?
questions.explanation: Gold can be beaten into extremely thin sheets.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which of the following is the most reactive metal?
questions.explanation: Potassium is high in the reactivity series.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A copper strip placed in iron sulphate solution shows no change because
options: copper is more reactive than iron
copper is less reactive than iron and cannot displace it
questions.explanation: Only a more reactive metal can displace another from its salt.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which non-metal is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Bromine is the only liquid non-metal.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Solder, used for welding electrical wires, is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Solder is lead and tin and has a low melting point.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Iron objects near the sea coast rust faster mainly because
options: salts in the moist air speed up corrosion
questions.explanation: Dissolved salts make the moisture a better conductor and speed up rusting.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is meant by the reactivity series of metals?
questions.answer: The reactivity series is a list of metals arranged in decreasing order of their reactivity, from the most reactive, such as potassium, to the least reactive, such as gold.
keyPoints: Order from most to least reactive
questions.explanation: It predicts which metal can displace another.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Differentiate between roasting and calcination.
questions.answer: In roasting, a sulphide ore is heated strongly in excess of air to form the oxide. In calcination, a carbonate ore is heated strongly in limited air or no air to form the oxide.
keyPoints: Roasting for sulphide ores in excess air
Calcination for carbonate ores in limited air
questions.explanation: Both convert the ore into a metal oxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The chemical name of CH3CH2OH is
questions.explanation: A two-carbon alcohol is ethanol.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The number of carbon atoms in a molecule of propane is
questions.explanation: The prefix prop- means three carbons.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The number of hydrogen atoms in a molecule of pentane (C5H12) is
questions.explanation: Alkanes have the formula CnH(2n+2), so for n = 5 it is 12.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The burning of carbon compounds in oxygen with the release of heat and light is called
questions.explanation: Combustion is rapid oxidation with heat and light.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Ethanol is oxidised by alkaline potassium permanganate to give
questions.explanation: Oxidising agents convert ethanol to ethanoic acid.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Detergents are better than soaps for washing in hard water because
options: their calcium and magnesium salts are soluble, so no scum forms
questions.explanation: Detergents do not form insoluble scum with the ions of hard water.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is a functional group? Give two examples.
questions.answer: A functional group is an atom or group of atoms in a carbon compound that decides its chemical properties. Examples are -OH (alcohol) and -COOH (carboxylic acid).
keyPoints: Atom or group deciding chemical properties
questions.explanation: Compounds with the same functional group react similarly.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why are carbon compounds generally poor conductors of electricity?
questions.answer: Carbon compounds are formed by sharing of electrons, so they are made of neutral molecules and have no free ions or electrons to carry current.
questions.explanation: Conduction needs charged particles that can move.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Most of the digested food is absorbed in the
questions.explanation: The small intestine has villi and a rich blood supply for absorption.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The red pigment in red blood cells is
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin binds oxygen and gives blood its red colour.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: During heavy exercise the breathing rate increases because
options: muscle cells need more oxygen and produce more carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: A faster rate supplies oxygen and removes extra carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The windpipe is also called the
questions.explanation: The trachea is held open by rings of cartilage.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In pulmonary circulation, blood is taken from the heart to the
questions.explanation: Pulmonary circulation links the heart and the lungs.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Transport of sugars in the phloem (translocation) differs from transport of water in the xylem in that it
options: is a passive process by gravity only
uses energy to move sucrose into the phloem tissue
questions.explanation: Sucrose is loaded into phloem using energy from ATP.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What are enzymes?
questions.answer: Enzymes are biological catalysts, mostly proteins, that speed up chemical reactions in living organisms. For example, amylase digests starch.
keyPoints: Speed up reactions in the body
questions.explanation: Digestive enzymes break food down into small molecules.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How are oxygen and carbon dioxide exchanged in the alveoli?
questions.answer: The alveoli have very thin walls surrounded by capillaries. Oxygen from the air in the alveoli diffuses into the blood, and carbon dioxide diffuses from the blood into the alveoli to be breathed out.
questions.explanation: Gas exchange occurs by diffusion.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The pituitary is often called the master gland because it
questions.explanation: Pituitary hormones control other glands and body growth.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A reflex arc consists of a receptor, sensory neuron, spinal cord, motor neuron and an
questions.explanation: The effector, a muscle or gland, produces the response.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The pollen tube grows towards the ovule in response to chemicals. This movement is called
questions.explanation: Growth towards a chemical stimulus is chemotropism.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The plant hormone that helps in the ripening of fruits is
questions.explanation: Ethylene is a gaseous hormone for fruit ripening.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Cytokinins mainly promote
questions.explanation: Cytokinins are found in rapidly dividing tissues like fruits and seeds.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Animals use both nerves and hormones for control because
options: nerves can work only in the brain
nerve impulses are fast and short-lived, whereas hormones act more slowly and their effects last longer
questions.explanation: The two systems complement each other.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State the function of the cerebellum.
questions.answer: The cerebellum maintains the posture and balance of the body and coordinates voluntary movements such as walking in a straight line or picking up a pencil.
questions.explanation: It is part of the hindbrain.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Compare nervous control and hormonal control in animals.
questions.answer: Nervous control uses electrical impulses that travel along nerves and give quick, short-lived responses. Hormonal control uses chemicals carried by blood, which act more slowly but have longer-lasting effects.
keyPoints: Hormonal: chemicals in blood, slower, long-lasting
questions.explanation: The two systems work together.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A potato plant is grown commonly from its
questions.explanation: Each eye on a potato tuber can grow into a new plant.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: In human males, sperms are produced in the
questions.explanation: The testes make sperm and the hormone testosterone.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Reproduction is essential for a species, though not for the survival of an individual, because it
options: increases the lifespan of the individual
maintains the continuity of the species
questions.explanation: Without reproduction the species would die out as individuals die.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The release of an egg from the ovary is called
questions.explanation: Ovulation is release of a mature egg.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The normal period of pregnancy in humans is about
questions.explanation: The gestation period is about nine months.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Wind-pollinated flowers usually produce
options: light, dry pollen in very large quantities
questions.explanation: Large quantities of light pollen improve the chance of reaching a stigma.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is regeneration? Name an organism that shows it.
questions.answer: Regeneration is the ability of an organism to grow back lost parts or even a whole new individual from a piece. Planaria and Hydra show regeneration.
keyPoints: Example such as Planaria or Hydra
questions.explanation: Specialised cells make new tissues.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: How does the male gamete reach the egg in a flower after the pollen lands on the stigma?
questions.answer: The pollen grain grows a pollen tube through the style down to the ovary. The male gamete passes through the tube to the ovule, where it fuses with the egg cell.
keyPoints: Pollen tube grows through the style
Reaches the ovule in the ovary
questions.explanation: This completes fertilisation in flowers.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The genetic material in a cell is found mainly on the
questions.explanation: Genes are located on chromosomes in the nucleus.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Two heterozygous tall plants (Tt) are crossed. The chance that an offspring is dwarf is
questions.explanation: Only tt plants are dwarf, and they form one in four.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Two tall pea plants produce some dwarf offspring. The genotypes of the parents must be
questions.explanation: Both must carry the recessive allele to produce tt offspring, and they are tall, so both are Tt.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which process introduces small errors that cause variation?
questions.explanation: Inexact copying of DNA gives rise to variations.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A pair of contrasting forms of a gene is called
questions.explanation: Alleles are alternative forms of a gene, such as T and t.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A Tt pea plant is tall although it carries the t allele because
options: the t allele makes the plant tall
the dominant T masks the effect of t
questions.explanation: A dominant allele shows its effect even when only one copy is present.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is meant by variation?
questions.answer: Variation means the differences between the individuals of a species, such as in height, colour or other characteristics.
questions.explanation: Variation arises from sexual reproduction and errors in DNA copying.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Why was the garden pea a good choice for Mendel's experiments?
questions.answer: It has many easily seen contrasting traits, a short life cycle, produces many seeds, and can be self-pollinated or cross-pollinated in a controlled way.
keyPoints: Short life cycle and many seeds
questions.explanation: These features made the results easy to study.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately
questions.explanation: Light travels at about 300 000 km per second in vacuum.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: The magnification produced by a spherical mirror is given by
questions.explanation: m = h'/h = -v/u.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: An object is placed beyond 2F of a convex lens. The image formed is
options: real, inverted and diminished, between F and 2F
at the focus and highly diminished
questions.explanation: For an object beyond 2F, the image lies between F and 2F on the other side.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Which mirror has its principal focus behind the mirror?
questions.explanation: Reflected rays from a convex mirror appear to come from a point behind it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A ray of light enters a glass slab from air along the normal. It
questions.explanation: A ray along the normal is not deviated.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Refractive indices are about 1.33 for water, 1.5 for glass and 2.42 for diamond. Light travels slowest in
questions.explanation: The higher the refractive index, the slower the light.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: What is meant by magnification? Write the formula for a mirror.
questions.answer: Magnification is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, showing how much larger or smaller the image is. For a mirror, m = h'/h = -v/u.
keyPoints: Ratio of image height to object height
questions.explanation: A negative sign means a real, inverted image.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: State two differences between a real image and a virtual image.
questions.answer: A real image can be obtained on a screen, while a virtual image cannot. A real image is formed when light rays actually meet and is usually inverted, whereas a virtual image is formed by rays that only appear to meet and is erect.
keyPoints: Real image can be caught on a screen
Real is formed by actual meeting of rays
questions.explanation: The difference lies in whether the rays actually meet.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The optic nerve carries signals from the retina to the
questions.explanation: The brain interprets the electrical signals as an image.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

questions.explanation: Light from behind the observer is dispersed by raindrops in front.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: Which of the following is not mainly due to scattering of light?
questions.explanation: A rainbow is caused by refraction, dispersion and internal reflection in water drops.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The defect in which distant objects appear blurred is
questions.explanation: Myopia means a person sees near objects clearly but not distant ones.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: When we look at a distant object, the ciliary muscles
options: contract and the lens becomes thicker
contract and the lens becomes thinner
relax and the lens becomes thicker
relax and the lens becomes thinner
questions.explanation: A thin lens has a longer focal length and focuses distant objects.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: A rectangular glass slab does not produce a spectrum from white light because
options: the opposite faces are parallel, so the dispersed colours recombine
the glass absorbs all the colours
light does not refract in glass
the slab is too thin to bend light
questions.explanation: The second parallel face bends the colours back, so the emergent beam is white again.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: What is the function of the optic nerve?
questions.answer: The optic nerve carries the electrical signals produced in the retina to the brain, where they are interpreted as images.
questions.explanation: Seeing is completed in the brain.

questions.subject: science
questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: What is hypermetropia? State one cause.
questions.answer: Hypermetropia is a defect in which a person can see distant objects clearly but not nearby ones, since the image forms behind the retina. It is caused by a weak eye lens with a long focal length or an eyeball that is too short.
keyPoints: A cause such as a short eyeball
questions.explanation: A convex lens corrects it.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: A device used to change the resistance in a circuit is called a
questions.explanation: A rheostat is a variable resistor.

questions.subject: science
questions.q: Four resistors of 2 ohm each are connected in series. The equivalent resistance is
questions.explanation: In series the resistances add: 4 x 2 = 8 ohm.
